field.label: Enable Error Monitor
field.comment: Master switch. When off, no errors are captured and no emails are sent.

field.label: Auto-pause After Deploy (minutes)
field.comment: Default 5. Many deploys skip maintenance:enable; the resulting visitor/bot hits then flood the log with stale-cache noise. The module watches the mtime of pub/static/deployed_version.txt, generated/code and generated/metadata and suspends capture for this many minutes after each detected change (delta-based - only a strictly newer mtime triggers a pause, so a directory whose mtime simply looks recent does not silence capture forever). Set to 0 to disable. Diagnose with bin/magento panth:errormonitor:status.

field.label: Auto-Filter Sibling Module Operational Alerts
field.comment: Drops log lines matching [VendorModuleName] BLOCKED/REJECTED/DENIED ... - the family-wide alert convention used by sibling security / firewall modules in the Panth ecosystem. These are operational events ("we blocked something") rather than defects and pollute the error grid. Recommended ON.

field.label: Ignore Errors Matching
field.comment: One substring per line, matched case-insensitively. An error is dropped at capture time if the substring appears anywhere in its message, file path, error class, or stack trace. Use this to silence a whole noisy module (e.g. Vendor_Module, vendor/somevendor/) or a specific message family (e.g. Deprecated Functionality:, Page URL:).

field.label: Max Stored Occurrences per Error Group
field.comment: Default 50. Detailed occurrence rows (URL, user agent, stack trace) kept per error group, so one repeating error cannot fill the database. What happens at the limit is set below. Set to 0 for no limit.

field.label: When the Occurrence Limit Is Reached
field.comment: Default: keep the oldest rows (the behaviour of 1.6.x): once a group holds the maximum number of rows, further occurrences only raise the occurrence count, Last Seen and the hourly counters, and no stored row is deleted. "Keep the newest rows" replaces the oldest rows so the latest stack traces are always available. The daily summary counts occurrences from exact hourly counters in both modes.

field.label: Ignore Errors from Bots/Crawlers
field.comment: Default Yes. Storefront JS reports and PHP errors raised during a web request whose User-Agent matches the list below are dropped. When set to No they are recorded with an is_bot flag in the occurrence context, and the daily summary shows the bot share per group.

field.label: Bot User-Agent Patterns
field.comment: One pattern per line, matched case-insensitively against the User-Agent. Plain words match as substrings (e.g. bingbot); the single word bot only matches as a separate word or a name ending in "bot" followed by /, ;, ) or - (so phone and app names such as CUBOT or RobotApp are not treated as bots); anything else is used as a regular expression (e.g. ^Mozilla/5\.0 \(compatible; Foo). Each line is tested on its own; invalid expressions are skipped, and if every line is invalid the default list is used. Leave empty to disable bot detection.

field.label: Leave Bot-only Groups out of the Summary Email
field.comment: A group whose occurrences in the last 24 hours all came from bots is not listed in the email; the email footer counts how many were hidden.

field.label: Ignore Known Browser and Third-party Noise
field.comment: Default Yes. Drops errors that are not caused by the store: the Outlook / Safe Links scanner (Object Not Found Matching Id), private-mode and full localStorage errors from customer-data.js / js.storage.js, Script error. without a stack trace, and errors from browser extensions. The same rules hide matching groups that were stored earlier from the summary email.

field.label: Noise Patterns
field.comment: One rule per line; a rule is a case-insensitive regular expression tested against the error message. Prefix it with file:, stack:, source: (file or stack trace) or any: (message, file and stack) to test another field, or nostack: to match the message only when there is no stack trace. Join conditions with && to require all of them, e.g. source:customer-data && message:SecurityError. Invalid rules are skipped.

field.label: Capture PHP Exceptions
field.comment: Records exceptions and errors that Magento writes to the system log.

field.label: Minimum Severity to Capture
field.comment: Only errors at this level or more severe are stored.

field.label: Coalesce Window (seconds)
field.comment: When the same error repeats, only one database write is made per group within this window; the rest are counted in cache and folded into the total. Protects the database and binary log from a single high-frequency error. Default 60. Set to 0 to write every occurrence.

field.label: GraphQL Client Errors
field.comment: Errors that GraphQL marks as client-safe (isClientSafe()), such as Cannot query field ... on type ... or address validation messages, are caused by the request, not by the server. Default: do not record. "Record as notice" stores them with severity notice and keeps them out of the summary email.

field.label: Capture Storefront JS Errors
field.comment: Injects a tiny, CSP-safe collector that reports uncaught JS errors and promise rejections.

field.label: Sample Rate (%)
field.comment: Percentage of page views whose JS errors are reported (0-100). 0 stops reporting. Lower this on very high-traffic sites.

field.label: Max Reports per IP per Minute
field.comment: Server-side rate limit. Requests beyond this are silently dropped to prevent abuse/flooding.

field.label: Max Report Body Size (KB)
field.comment: Larger payloads are rejected before parsing.

field.label: Max New JS Error Groups per Hour
field.comment: Default 100. Store-wide limit on how many new, never-seen JavaScript error groups the storefront collector may create per clock hour. Beyond it, new JS errors are dropped (errors already in the log are still counted) and one warning per hour is written to var/log/system.log. Protects the database from floods of fake reports. Set to 0 for no limit.

field.label: Send Email Alerts
field.comment: Alerts are sent by cron, never synchronously. Each error group is emailed at most once per day.

field.label: Daily Summary Hour (0-23, UTC)
field.comment: Hour of day (UTC) the once-per-day summary is sent, e.g. 23 = end of day. The email lists groups with occurrences in the 24 hours before sending and shows times in the store timezone. The summary is sent at most ONCE per day, regardless of how many errors fire - there is no "every N hours" mode.

field.label: Recipient Email(s)
field.comment: Comma- or newline-separated. Invalid addresses are skipped.

field.label: Minimum Severity to Email
field.comment: Lower-severity errors are still stored, just not emailed.

field.label: Max Error Groups per Email
field.comment: Hard cap on how many error groups a single email lists. Prevents huge emails during incidents.

field.label: Store Client IP
field.comment: When off, no IP address is stored on error events.

field.label: Anonymise IP
field.comment: Masks the last octet (IPv4) / last 80 bits (IPv6) before storing, for GDPR compliance.

field.label: Keep Individual Events (days)
field.comment: Occurrence rows older than this are deleted by the daily cleanup cron. Group aggregates are kept.

field.label: Keep Resolved Groups (days)
field.comment: Resolved error groups not seen for this many days are removed entirely.

field.label: Keep Unresolved Groups (days)
field.comment: Groups still in status New that have not occurred for this many days are removed by the daily cleanup, together with their events. Ignored groups are never removed by this setting. 0 keeps unresolved groups until an administrator resolves or deletes them.
